objective: Prove: (1) with non-constant uniform signs every Cayley law's knot is satisfied by the constant assignment; (2) a simple cubic triple system whose automorphisms are transitive on points and on lines has an incidence graph with no nontrivial tight cut (a brace), by a minimal-shore counting argument; (3) hence, by THREEFOLD-SPACES-20261030-001A's dictionary and McCuaig's theorem, the only non-2-colourable such system is the Fano plane, so the Fano plane is the only uniform law whose knot is unsatisfiable. Check on a census of Cayley laws with controls (the 13-point Fano splice has a tight cut and is not line-transitive).
status: Proved 2026-11-07: non-constant uniform signs are satisfied by the constant assignment; a simple cubic triple system transitive on points and lines has a brace for its incidence graph (two translates of a smallest tight shore share at most one point, and counting forces a two-point shore holding a line); so by Seymour's dictionary and McCuaig's theorem the Fano plane is the only uniform law whose knot is unsatisfiable. Census of 439 simple Cayley laws (orders 3-720) agrees.
title: Uniform contradictions: the brace lemma and McCuaig
